name: inprocess-obi-apb-axi4lite-tlul-mixed-three-protocol-f1f4
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU reaches three independently addressed MMIO targets, each speaking a different protocol, in one process: the PULP timer at 0x40001000 (APB3, the one F5 target), the ZipCPU axiluart at 0x40002000 (AXI4-Lite) and the OpenTitan rv_timer at 0x40003000 (TL-UL). Every target states its own protocol from its own artifact, each case states the protocol of the target it was routed to, and the summary states each target's protocol and bridge.
notes: Three protocols in one build: target 0 is the PULP timer at 0x40001000 behind the real apb3_mmio_bridge (apb/3), target 1 is the ZipCPU axiluart at 0x40002000 behind the real axi4_lite_mmio_bridge (axi4-lite/1), target 2 is the OpenTitan rv_timer at 0x40003000 behind the real beat_to_tlul adapter (tl-ul/1).

The three windows are disjoint: 0x40001000..0x40002000, 0x40002000..0x40002010 and 0x40003000..0x40004000, none overlaps the RAM image 0x10000..0x30000, and all clear the 4 GiB bound. The host's routing table is derived from the generated per-target traits, not from a device name or an address list.

Registers: TIMER0_COUNT(0), TIMER0_CTRL(4), TIMER0_CMP(8) on the APB3 timer; SETUP(0, rw), FIFO_STATUS(4, ro), RXREG(8, rw, read pops), TXREG(12, rw, write pushes) on the AXI4-Lite UART; CTRL(0x4, rw) and COMPARE_LOWER0_0(0x118, rw) on the TL-UL rv_timer.

Only target 0 declares F5 facts, through configs/behaviors/pulp_timer_f5.json: irq_o[0], a 16-tick pulse, trigger writes [[4,0],[8,0],[0,4294967295]] and the TIMER0_COUNT status word at offset 0. The AXI4-Lite target declares no F5 behavior, and an AXI4-Lite target that declared the four facts would be refused by name (unsupported-f5:target-protocol-not-run:axi4-lite:...), because no real AXI4-Lite F5 run exists. The summary states target1_f5 no and target2_f5 no.

Each target is sampled on its own protocol: APB3 psel/penable/pready, AXI4-Lite AW/W/B/AR/R, TL-UL A/D handshakes. A case routed to one target must leave the other two targets at 0 reads and 0 writes; the host prints per-target counters on every case line.

No DMA is declared: the route criterion is the APB3 one, and a route to an AXI4-Lite or TL-UL target is refused by name (unsupported-dma-route:apb3-target-only:...). F6 is refused as unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:APB3+AXI4-Lite+TL-UL.
The three profiles declare 50 MHz each, so one host tick drives all four models; assume_single_clock states that rather than leaving it implicit.
